To compute ${g}^{′}(x),$ we first make the substitution $u={x}^{3}$ and then we apply the chain rule, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{g}^{′}(x) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}{\int }_{0}^{{x}^{3}}({t}^{3}-2t)\,\text{d}t \\  & =\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}\cdot \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}u}{\int }_{0}^{u}({t}^{3}-2t)\,\text{d}t\end{aligned}
$$

The integrand is continuous on $[0,u].$ Therefore, by FTC II, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{g}^{′}(x) & =\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}\cdot \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}u}{\int }_{0}^{u}({t}^{3}-2t)\,\text{d}t \\  & =\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}\cdot ({u}^{3}-2u) \\  & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}({x}^{3})\cdot (({x}^{3})^{3}-2({x}^{3})) \\  & =3{x}^{2}\cdot ({x}^{9}-2{x}^{3}) \\  & =3{x}^{2}({x}^{9}-2{x}^{3}).\end{aligned}
$$
